correctness.rationale: One length-k palindromic duplication corresponds bijectively to an inverse start where a 2k block is a palindrome. Two consecutive valid starts enforce a constant 2k+1-symbol overlap, and both deletion histories give the same parent; every consecutive run of valid starts therefore contributes at most one parent and gives upper bound ceil(m/2), m=n−k+1. For k≥3 with 4∤k, explicit period-four words (aabb)^ω when k odd or (abba)^ω when k≡2 mod4 have precisely the even valid starts and pairwise distinct inverse parents, attaining the bound for all n≥k. When m odd≥3, equality forces alternating valid starts 101...01, and composition of palindrome reflections at start separation 2 enforces global period four, leaving exactly q(q−1) distinct maximizing received words (a≠b). For 4|k and n=k+2, starts 0 and 2 force period four but deletion offsets k are period multiples, giving identical parents; adjacent valid starts also collide, hence maximum one. Independent full brute-force enumeration of all binary received words for k=3..7 and n through k+4 under length≤17 reproduced the maximum and odd-m maximizers; no finite check substitutes for the all-n proof.
